A_general.open_code_note: The public repository is Auth0’s local stdio MCP implementation for the same product. The supplied endpoint is a hosted HTTPS endpoint; the reviewed sources do not establish that this repository’s code runs there. The documented tool reference is used as the best available official evidence for the endpoint because endpoint-specific documentation and metadata were unavailable.
A_general.release_status: Beta (public implementation; endpoint-specific release status not found)
other_official_servers: The public repository documents a local stdio server launched through @auth0/auth0-mcp-server; no separate purpose or tool set for the supplied hosted endpoint was found.
Auth0 Docs MCP is a separate documentation-search service referenced at https://auth0.com/docs/mcp; it is not the tenant-management server.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official hosted reference names read and write operations but publishes no tool annotations. Public local tool definitions mark read-only tools with readOnlyHint true and write tools false; create/update/deploy actions are writes. destructiveHint and idempotentHint are defined for local tools, but hosted annotations are unknown. 2. Hosted confirmation enforcement was not found. Docs recommend reviewing suggested changes before confirming; local tool descriptions do not establish server-enforced confirmation. 3. Hosted scopes, roles, admin switches, allowlists, token lifetime, and revocation were not found because OAuth metadata requests failed. Product docs describe user authentication and permissions generally. 4. Hosted read-only modes, filters, environment separation, and region variants were not found. Local code supports --read-only and --tools; read-only takes priority over tool patterns. 5. Hosted response redaction and data boundaries are undocumented. Local code states it redacts sensitive fields such as client_secret and token as [REDACTED]. 6. Hosted rate limits, quotas, caps, truncation, and per-call costs were not found. Local code limits auth0_save_credentials_to_file to five calls per minute and caps auth0_list_logs take at 100 (default 50). 7. Hosted argument validation is unknown. Local server rejects arguments outside the declared input schema; individual handlers also validate parameters. 8. Hosted logging and telemetry are unknown. Local code sends tool usage and runtime properties to Heap unless AUTH0_MCP_ANALYTICS=false. 9. No vendor feedback/rating tools appear in the official 20-name list. Hosted upsell behavior is unknown. 10. Hosted instructions/skills were not found. Local tool descriptions include behavioral guidance; external Auth0 Agent Skills are documented separately. 11. Hosted memory/state behavior was not found. 12. Hosted architecture beyond this endpoint was not found; local implementation is a flat tool server. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, or script-execution tool appears in the official tool list.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: Official Auth0 tool reference exists at https://auth0.com/docs/get-started/auth0-mcp-server/auth0-mcp-tools-reference and names 20 tools; it states no total. No catalogue-only tools were added because catalogue pages describe the local stdio product variant, not verified tools of the supplied hosted endpoint. MCP100 reports 23 local tools (Applications 5, resource servers 4, Actions 5, Logs 2, Forms 4, plus local helpers); Agent Switchboard gives no tool count, and Vetted reports local stdio registry metadata rather than a tool count. The official local code includes three additional local-only helpers absent from the hosted docs list; those are not included here. E_aggregated.token_method: Hosted endpoint tool definitions and initialize instructions were unavailable; the public code is not confirmed to be the deployed hosted implementation. The official hosted docs provide names and prose descriptions but not verbatim tool schemas/instructions.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The hosted MCP reference covers only the listed application, API/resource-server, Action, log, and Form operations. It does not list user-management operations, application deletion, or a general raw Management API call. The public local code also does not define a user-management or delete-application tool. Humans can use the Auth0 Dashboard and Management API directly for operations beyond the documented MCP tool set; public REST documentation is not used as MCP schema evidence.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The official tool guide says: “Review before confirming: When Claude suggests changes, review them carefully before confirming.” This is client/user guidance; no hosted server enforcement was documented. The public local code enforces schema allowlisting but not a human approval step.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Auth0’s announcement says MCP operations are secured through OAuth 2.0 and scoped permissions. The local README says sensitive values such as client_secret and token are redacted as [REDACTED]. The hosted endpoint’s token handling and redaction behavior could not be verified. The local implementation sends usage analytics to Heap by default, with AUTH0_MCP_ANALYTICS=false as the opt-out.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The product announcement describes secure management without handing over raw API tokens or direct Management API access. The local README says beta software is provided as is without warranties and is not recommended for production workloads.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The OAuth and security claims are documented for the product, but endpoint-specific implementation evidence is unavailable. Public local code implements sensitive-field redaction, tool argument allowlisting, and optional analytics opt-out. The recommendation to review before confirmation remains client/user guidance in the reviewed evidence.

contradictions: The hosted tools reference documents 20 tools. The public local implementation and third-party MCP100 listing show 23 tools, including local-only auth0_save_credentials_to_file, auth0_onboarding, and auth0_get_quickstart_guide; their availability on the supplied hosted endpoint is unverified.
The getting-started documentation mentions verifying auth0_delete_application, but the official tools reference and public local tool definitions contain no delete-application tool.

The public local code and README mention saving credentials and onboarding helpers, which are absent from the official hosted tools reference. The reference’s Form list also omits a publish-form tool; the public local code contains no publish-form tool either.
observations_for_research: The official product documentation describes a local stdio server, while the researched object is a global hosted HTTPS endpoint; public evidence does not tie the hosted deployment to the repository implementation.

The official hosted tools reference gives names and natural-language descriptions but does not publish schemas or annotations; parameter details were inferred from same-product public local code and may not match the hosted endpoint.
The documentation recommends client-side review before confirmation; this is distinct from a server-enforced approval mechanism, for which hosted evidence was not found.
